Boston's researchers suggest the surge in sponsorships is at least partly strategic, driven by election-minded Republican lawmakers courting anti-vaccine constituents who fashion themselves as champions of "medical freedom." "Our work shows that state lawmakers affiliated with the Republican party are responsible for the overwhelming majority of anti-vaccine bills introduced in recent years," study corresponding author Dr. Matt Motta said in a statement. "While the majority of these bills do not actually pass, it's important to remember that we live in an increasingly connected world—one in which low vaccine coverage in one part of the country can get people sick thousands of miles away." ranked_evidence.title: Traumatic Brain Injuries Spike 26% as Veterans Push More Research, Funding - Military.com
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Traumatic Brain Injuries Spike 26% as Veterans Push More Research, Funding. The number of TBI cases reported to the VA database grew by 26 percent between 2021 and 2025. Veteran advocacy groups have called for more funding and research into traumatic brain injuries (TBI) after newly released data from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) documented a surge in reported cases. The new VA data shows that the number of cases of TBI reported to the VA grew by 26% between 2021 and 2025, with more than 28,000 cases a year. The nonprofit Disabled American Veterans (DAV) and military health research group Invisible Wounds Foundation, in a joint statement, called on Congress to "act now" to fund "research to prevent, diagnose and treat TBI," which occurs when a sudden blow to the head causes damage to the brain. Seizures, caused by a condition called post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) that develops after a TBI, can be prevented by treating patients with chemicals derived from the gut microbiome, according to new research from Texas A&M University's Naresh K.

ranked_evidence.title: Somalia hands over its citizen to Kash Patel-led FBI team to face charges in $250 million COVID child-feeding fraud case - Business Insider Africa
ranked_evidence.snippet: # Somalia hands over its citizen to Kash Patel-led FBI team to face charges in $250 million COVID child-feeding fraud case. Somalia has handed over one of its citizens to a Kash Patel-led FBI team to face charges in a $250 million COVID-era fraud case involving taxpayer-funded resources intended to provide meals to children in need, nearly four years after American authorities issued a warrant for his arrest. * Somalia extradited Abdikerm Abdelahi Eidleh to the US to face 31 charges in a $250 million COVID-era child nutrition fraud case. * Eidleh, seen as a key figure in the 'Feeding Our Future' scandal, was located and lawfully surrendered in Somalia nearly four years after his indictment. * Eidleh’s capture demonstrates expanding Somalia-US legal cooperation and is a landmark in one of the largest pandemic-related fraud prosecutions in US history. Abdikerm Abdelahi Eidleh, 42, was transferred to Minnesota on July 16, 2026, after what the US Justice Department described as his lawful surrender in Somalia.
